WHERE WE ARE TODAY

LOCAL BUILD · 0.1.0

Small beginnings.
Clear intentions.

Monitoring is implemented locally. Charging support is still being qualified. Here’s an honest look at the current build.

Implemented locally

Your battery, in view

Live monitoring, seven-day history, CSV exports, settings, and opt-in alerts. Readings vary by Mac; unavailable values are shown as unavailable.

Being qualified

Apple’s 80% charge limit

A trusted-shortcut workflow is integrated for one qualified Mac and macOS target. The setting lab passed; end-to-end app, cutoff, and lifecycle checks are still pending. Confirmation and returning to 100% are manual.

Not available yet

Custom charging controls

Custom charge bands, discharge cutoffs, and temperature-based charging control remain unavailable. There is no public download yet.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

The finer details.

A little context before StatBatt finds a place in your menu bar.

Can I download StatBatt?

StatBatt is currently a local development build. A signed and notarized public release is not available. This page introduces the app and its current progress.

Which Macs is it being built for?

Apple silicon MacBooks. The app targets macOS 15 or later, but current qualification covers one Apple silicon device on macOS 27.0.1. Older macOS versions, other devices, and Intel Macs have not been qualified.

Does StatBatt control charging?

The current build includes a trusted Apple 80% shortcut setup and app workflow on an exact qualified target. Full app and charging-behavior checks are pending. It does not offer custom thresholds, intentional discharge, or automatic temperature protection. The Apple limit persists after quitting; restoring 100% requires a manual change in Battery settings.

Where does my battery history go?

It stays on your Mac. StatBatt keeps seven days of one-minute summaries in local storage. You can pause recording, export a CSV, or clear the history from the app. The current build has no cloud account or analytics service.

Are health and temperature readings exact?

Health and battery temperature are estimates when available, not a battery diagnosis. Advanced readings depend on the device and macOS version. StatBatt labels estimates and missing readings so you can tell what your Mac is actually reporting.
